flows.description: Supplies layered config and secrets at startup
Runs a due job's shell command unattended
Wires session access into ACP server
Daemon dispatches a turn to the agent loop
Wires session access into aegis mcp-serve
TUI delegates API calls to the HTTP client

threats.title: Terminal control-sequence injection
threats.description: Streamed model text may contain ANSI/OSC control sequences manipulating the terminal before rendering.

threats.title: Large stream render stall
threats.description: An extremely large single streamed chunk could stall rendering.

threats.title: Token in Client memory
threats.description: The bearer token resides in Client's process memory for its lifetime.

threats.title: No auth rate limiting
threats.description: No rate limiting/alerting on repeated invalid bearer-token attempts.

threats.title: server.addr misconfiguration
threats.description: server.addr configurable to non-loopback with no validation/warning.

threats.title: Unencrypted loopback traffic
threats.description: Client-Server traffic unencrypted over loopback.

threats.title: Unbounded concurrent runs
threats.description: Malicious/runaway client could open unbounded concurrent runs or SSE connections.

threats.title: Local token bypass via /ui
threats.description: Any local process can mint+exchange a page token for the real bearer token.

threats.title: Conversation content sent to cloud
threats.description: Full conversation content forwarded to configured provider with no redaction.

threats.title: No local-model budget ceiling
threats.description: No token/dollar budget ceiling for local models.

threats.title: LSP arbitrary binary
threats.description: lsp tool spawns config-specified binary with no allowlist.

threats.title: Unmarked web content injection
threats.description: web_fetch/web_search content has no untrusted-content marker.

threats.title: Auto mode no per-call confirmation
threats.description: In auto mode every execute tool runs with no per-call confirmation.
threats.mitigation: build mode requires approval; contextual/rule gates still apply.

threats.title: PersonaToolGate advisory only
threats.description: PersonaToolGate warns/allows rather than blocking.

threats.title: Rule bypass via shell metachars
threats.description: Loosely-scoped allow rule could be widened via shell metacharacters.

threats.title: Persona prompt injection
threats.description: Persona .md content injected verbatim into system prompt.

threats.title: Persona mode/rule escalation
threats.description: Loaded persona could raise permission mode or add allow rules.

threats.title: Skill prompt injection
threats.description: Skill .md content injected verbatim into system prompt.

threats.title: Guard fail-open no signal
threats.description: Guard transport failure fails open with no distinct audit signal.
threats.mitigation: Ambiguous verdicts fail closed by design.

threats.title: Installer script unverified
threats.description: Installer scripts invoke shell with unaudited arg construction.

threats.title: DAST target scope
threats.description: DAST/recon scans could target arbitrary network hosts.

threats.title: Unattended cron exec no gate
threats.description: Cron jobs fire shell commands with no permission gate/approval.

threats.title: No cron audit trail
threats.description: Job.Command stored with no dedicated execution audit trail.

threats.title: Swarm shared budget exhaustion
threats.description: Sub-agents share one budget tracker; one agent can exhaust it.

threats.title: Sub-agent gate bypass (P10.1)
threats.description: Sub-agents previously bypassed parent's contextual/rule gates.

threats.title: MCP scan bypass
threats.description: Opt-in scan_output is regex-based and bypassable.

threats.title: MCP output unmarked (baseline)
threats.description: Without marking, compromised MCP server output indistinguishable from instructions.

threats.title: mcp-serve no auth
threats.description: handleToolsCall performs no authentication check.
threats.mitigation: Sessions default to plan mode; auto_approve required for actions.

threats.title: ACP no auth
threats.description: methodAuthenticate is a no-op stub.

threats.title: Sandbox silent fallback
threats.description: Non-strict fallback to local unsandboxed execution on backend failure.
threats.mitigation: cfg.Strict makes this a hard failure.

threats.title: Config secret hardcoding risk
threats.description: Nothing prevents hardcoding a literal secret in config.yaml.
threats.mitigation: gitignore default + env-only API keys + redaction.

threats.title: .env no Windows ACL
threats.description: No Windows ACL hardening on .aegis/.env unlike daemon.token.

threats.title: Cloud outage no fallback
threats.description: Cloud outage/rate-limit halts sessions with no automatic fallback.

threats.title: Ollama plaintext traffic
threats.description: Local Ollama traffic typically unencrypted plain HTTP.

threats.title: SessionStore plaintext DB
threats.description: SQLite DB plaintext, no encryption at rest, no Windows ACL hardening.

threats.title: CheckpointStore plaintext
threats.description: Per-turn snapshots stored unencrypted on disk.

threats.title: Memory file tampering
threats.description: Memory files directly editable to inject false learned content.

threats.title: Mailbox plaintext files
threats.description: Inter-agent messages are plaintext files readable by same OS user.

threats.title: Anthropic cloud data exposure
threats.description: Conversation content sent to Anthropic with no redaction.

threats.title: Anthropic outage
threats.description: Full Anthropic outage stalls sessions pinned to that provider.

threats.title: OpenAI-compatible cloud data exposure
threats.description: Same cross-cloud exposure risk when configured against cloud OpenAI.

threats.title: MCP server content manipulation
threats.description: Malicious/compromised MCP server can return injected instructions.

threats.title: Tool args sent to MCP server
threats.description: Tool-call args with sensitive data sent unconditionally to configured MCP server.

threats.title: GitHub PR content leak
threats.description: PR titles/bodies not inspected for secrets before publishing.
threats.mitigation: git.go allowlist/denylist does not inspect PR body.

threats.title: Unmarked web content (external view)
threats.description: Fetched web content re-enters context with no untrusted marker.

threats.title: SSRF baseline
threats.description: Without validation, web_fetch/web_search could reach internal-only services.

threats.title: Docker socket privilege equivalence
threats.description: Docker/Podman socket access equivalent to local-root/administrator.
threats.mitigation: Only ExecutionSandbox's fallback warning; no rootless enforcement.

findings.title: Local process can obtain the daemon's real bearer token via the pre-auth /ui page-token flow
aegis mcp-serve and the ACP server accept commands from any local process with no authentication
Scheduled cron jobs execute unattended shell commands with no permission gate or approval
web_fetch/web_search content re-enters the model's context with no untrusted-content marker
Persona and skill .md files are injected into the system prompt with no sanitization
Docker/Podman socket access grants the daemon local-root-equivalent privilege
lsp tool spawns a config-specified binary with no allowlist or verification
server.addr can be configured to a non-loopback address with no validation or warning
Conversation content is sent to cloud LLM providers with no redaction or DLP step
Opt-in MCP output injection scan is regex-based and easily bypassed
No rate limiting or alerting on repeated invalid bearer-token attempts
Tool-call arguments are sent unconditionally to whichever MCP server is configured
GitHub PR titles/bodies are not inspected for secrets before publishing
Sub-agents in a swarm share a single budget tracker, allowing one runaway agent to exhaust it for all
OpenAIAdapter traffic to a local Ollama endpoint is typically unencrypted
OutputGuard's fail-open behavior produces no distinct audit signal when validation is skipped
TerminalUI does not sanitize ANSI/OSC control sequences in streamed model output
SSRF-safe outbound HTTP dialer for web_fetch/web_search (existing control)
Always-on MCP output provenance wrapping (existing control)
Sub-agent permission-gate parity fix (existing control)
Sandbox strict-mode hard-fail on backend unavailability (existing control)
Rule-engine anti-bypass protections and advisory-by-design persona tool gate (existing control)
Persona mode/rule escalation guard (existing control)
Run/connection resource ceilings and tool-call loop detection (existing control)
Security-scan target allow-list with literal-string host matching (existing control)
Provider failover/retry for cloud LLM outages (existing control)
Secret handling hygiene: env-only API keys, gitignored project config, redacted debug output (existing control)
Terminal render wrap-cache and scroll-follow for large streamed content (existing control)
Local data stores lack the Windows ACL hardening applied to daemon.token
Memory files can be directly edited to inject persistent false learned content
Security-scanner installer script argument construction was not fully verified
Client-Server traffic is unencrypted plain HTTP over loopback
Bearer token persists in Client process memory for the process lifetime
Cron job commands have no execution audit trail distinct from ordinary tool-call tracing
Mailbox file-permission restriction (existing control)
